summary: Luna & Fern writes like its founder Mia talks: a warm, unhurried friend who knows a lot about skin. Emails are calm, honest and specific, with gentle humour and zero pressure, and every claim is about how a product feels or what it does, never about fixing flaws.
audience: US women 25–45 with sensitive or reactive skin who want a simple, kind routine and distrust hype.

tone_by_email_type.tone: Relaxed and generous; the discount is mentioned plainly, urgency is soft and factual ("ends Sunday at midnight").
Personal origin story from Mia, reassuring, with a small no-rush gift.
No pressure; answers the likely questions and offers to talk.
Chatty studio diary with small confessions and Q&A.
Quietly proud; tells the making-of story, then the benefits.
Missed-you warmth, a gift, and an honest invitation to say why they left.

mechanics.sentence_length: Short to medium sentences (8–18 words), with the occasional two-word fragment for rhythm ("Promise.").
mechanics.person: First person singular from Mia ("I"), "we" for the studio, always addressing "you".
mechanics.capitalization: Sentence case everywhere, including subject lines and headlines.
mechanics.punctuation: Em dashes are common. At most one exclamation point per email and never in subject lines.
mechanics.emoji: Almost never. At most a single 🌿 in newsletters; none in promos.
mechanics.formatting: One-to-three-sentence paragraphs, short product lists as 'Name — benefit', a single soft button.

patterns: Warm metaphor tied to the product ("your skin's new bedtime story")
subject_lines.typical_length: 25–45 characters, sentence case, no emoji or exclamation points
examples: Meet Night Balm, your skin's new bedtime story

patterns: Adds the concrete detail the subject withholds (dates, no code needed)
Reassurance or a hint of what's inside
examples: Our bestsellers are on quiet sale until Sunday — no code needed.
It's been a while. Here's what's new, and a little something to welcome you back.

sections: price and how long it lasts

patterns: Three or four words, soft and specific
Often uses 'ritual' or names the benefit

sign_off: Love, Mia (sometimes followed by 'Founder, Luna & Fern')
dos: Describe how products feel on the skin
Mention fragrance-free / sensitive-skin testing when relevant
donts: Promise to erase, reverse or fix anything
Use ALL CAPS, countdown panic or 'LAST CHANCE'
Use exclamation points in subject lines
Use clinical jargon without explaining it
